title: Operator entropy guard: detect & auto-fix post-upgrade config skew causing nodeagent restart loops
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a private/VPC customer upgrade (helm/operator) we observed a post-upgrade churn where nodeagent pods enter restart loops and controllers rapidly requeue the same CRs. Root cause appears to be a subtle config/schema entropy introduced by a CRD->CR conversion race combined with Helm post-upgrade ordering. This ticket implements an "entropy guard" in the operator and a short hotfix release to automatically detect the skew, apply a safe transformation to in-cluster CRs, and provide an automated safe-rollback path for affected clusters.

Background: Customer ACME Bank reported that after applying operator v2.3.1 via helm in their VPC/on-prem cluster, several inference nodeagent processes restarted repeatedly and pods servicing customer inference requests degraded until the operator was manually rolled back. Initial triage shows controller log lines about "unknown field 'runtimeHints' in v1alpha1.InferenceConfig" followed by immediate requeue with exponential backoff. The Helm upgrade included a CRD conversion + values change that changed defaulting logic for nodeagent configs. In some clusters the CRs were left in a mixed state where an annotation used by the leader election controller was present but with an incompatible JSON blob.

Goals:
- Detect clusters where the CR spec/annotation blob is incompatible with new operator version without causing additional churn.
- Provide an automated in-cluster migration that sanitizes the offending annotation and reconciles CRs with backoff tuning to avoid watch storms.
- Ship a minimal operator hotfix (v2.3.2) and a companion helm patch that adds preflight checks and an opt-in upgrade-hook to sanitize CRs before post-upgrade reconcile.
- Publish runbook and ensure we have monitoring/alerting to rapidly identify remaining affected clusters.

Proposed technical approach:
1) Entropy guard controller: add a low-impact controller that runs once-per-CR at upgrade time (driven by the helm post-upgrade hook or operator leader config). The controller computes a fast hash of critical config fields and annotations (checksum/config style). If this checksum matches an incompatible legacy shape, it performs a safe transformation: remove legacy annotation, set explicit default values, and annotate the CR with a migration stamp. The transformation is idempotent and logged as a single reconciliation event.
2) Reconcile backoff & compact retry: operator will adopt a short-term exponential backoff cap and a per-CR in-flight guard to avoid global requeue storms. Add metrics: operator_reconcile_spikes, operator_migrations_applied, nodeagent_restart_rate.
3) Helm changes: add a pre-upgrade validation hook that runs a lightweight kubectl/python script to detect CRs with legacy shapes and fail the upgrade with a clear message and auto-link to the runbook unless the admin passes --set operator.allow-legacy-migration=true. Also add the post-upgrade hook that triggers the entropy guard when the chart is installed with migration enabled.
4) Hotfix release: prepare operator v2.3.2 containing the entropy guard and backoff improvements. Patch release notes will include rollback instructions and a one-command remediation script for SEs to run (kubectl apply -f remediation-job.yaml).

Runbook / customer remediation flow (high-level):
- If customer is actively degraded: advise immediate helm rollback to v2.3.0 (chart rollback) to stop churn. If rollback is not possible (policy), apply the remediation job (one-off Kubernetes job included in release) that sanitizes CRs.
- After remediation, restart affected nodeagents sequentially with a configured grace window (default 30s) and verify reconcilers are stable.
- If operator logs show continued unknown-field errors, collect CR manifests, operator logs, and call for escalation to SRE.

Observability and alerts:
- Add detection query: sum by(cluster) (increase(nodeagent_restart_count[10m])) and alert if > X threshold.
- Create an anomaly detector for operator_reconcile_spikes where > 5x baseline over 5 minutes.
- Dashboard: Post-upgrade health panel showing migration_applied, unknown_field_errors, and average reconcile duration.

Acceptance criteria:
- v2.3.2 binary + chart released to staging and smoke-tested on infra clusters without causing spurious migration on healthy clusters.
- >= 1 customer cluster with prior failure pattern successfully remediated in staging and in one pilot customer cluster.
- Runbook documented with rollback, remediation job, and contact path for SE escalation.
- New alerts firing for both restart-rate and reconcile-spike anomalies.

Notes and links:
- Confluence investigation doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Post-Upgrade+Entropy+Investigation
- Draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OPS/Operator+Entropy+Guard+Runbook
- GitHub hotfix PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/operator/pull/1897
- SE escalation thread: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-runbook-link
comments: 2025-02-10 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage with ACME SE. Collected operator logs and CR dumps. Observed 'unknown field' errors correlated with restart spikes. Customer requested immediate mitigation and SLA review.

2025-02-11 - Carlos Mendes: Reproduced failure in a replica cluster using the same helm values. Confirmed CR annotation contains legacy JSON blob that newer schemas treat as unknown. Created minimal repro script and added to PR #1897.
2025-02-12 - Priya Shah (SRE): Suggested adding operator-level backoff cap to reduce requeue storm. Implemented metric operator_reconcile_spikes. Added smoke tests for reconciliation stability.

2025-02-13 - Carlos Mendes: Prototype entropy guard implemented (migration annotated as migration.redwood.io/v1). Running migration job on staging cluster succeeded without pod churn. Preparing release branch.

2025-02-14 - Legal/Support: ACME Bank requested timeline and asks for hotfix notes. Provided ETA for v2.3.2 tomorrow and drafted customer-facing advisory. Escalation team created billing/shutdown lock as precaution.
2025-02-15 - Product (Evan Liu): Approved opt-in helm preflight behavior for disruptive upgrades. Requesting that default chart remains conservative (migration opt-in).
2025-02-16 - Carlos Mendes: Pushed PR 1897 with tests, docs, and a remediation job manifest. CI failing on one e2e timeout; investigating flakiness in reconcile test harness.

2025-02-17 - QA (Marta Gomez): Verified hotfix in staging clusters. Found an edge case where annotation exists but has semantically valid shape leading migration to be skipped — added test to ensure idempotence.
2025-02-18 - Aisha Patel: Running customer pilot with ACME after manual approval. Monitoring alerting and nodeagent restart rates. Next steps: release v2.3.2 and schedule postmortem asap.
hotfix_release_notes: v2.3.2: Add entropy guard controller to sanitize legacy annotations, cap reconcile backoff to avoid watch storms, introduce helm preflight check and post-upgrade migration hook. See PR #1897 for details.
